primitives.name: Draw Uncertainty
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper defines team-level **draw uncertainty** as the standard deviation of qualification probability across random draws, estimated by 1,000 random draws × 1,000 outcome simulations each, with independent Poisson outcomes derived from Elo expectancy and bootstrap confidence intervals.

primitives.assumptions: Independent Poisson outcomes, fixed Elo ratings, uniform draw distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When draw randomness dominates over seeding accuracy or format structure.

This SD_i captures how much a team's chance of qualifying varies due to random fixture assignment. It is computed via Monte Carlo simulation: 1,000 random draws × 1,000 outcome simulations per draw, assuming independent Poisson outcomes based on Elo expectancies. The dual nature of this primitive lies in its ability to separate two sources of variation: format effects (e.g., group stage vs playoff structure) and seeding accuracy (e.g., whether teams are ranked by true strength). The decomposition method re-runs simulations under perfect seeding and no playoffs to isolate the pure format effect. This reveals that most draw uncertainty reduction in the new Champions League format stems from improved robustness to seeding errors, not the format itself. Failure modes include ignoring score correlations, assuming fixed Elo ratings, and restricting findings to UCL-specific constraints.
